title: Keep runtime-owned properties out of configuration binding
goal: Bind configuration into a model while preserving selected runtime-owned properties, even when matching input keys are present.

selectionNotes: ConfigurationIgnore governs configuration binding only; it does not redact providers or affect JSON serialization.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The newer comparison uses .NET 11 framework contracts.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build against .NET 11 references; the exact RC2 SDK is a verification baseline.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical sample language mode; no preview language syntax is used.

frameworks: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 11 shared framework; full implementations, not only base-framework abstractions.
platforms: Any platform supporting the declared .NET/shared-framework combination; managed checks executed on Windows x64.
prerequisites: Console project: TargetFramework=net11.0, LangVersion=15.0, Nullable=enable, ImplicitUsings=enable, FrameworkReference Microsoft.AspNetCore.App. Exact imports and registration steps are in the body.
constraints: ConfigurationIgnore governs configuration binding only; it does not redact providers or affect JSON serialization.
No external account, provisioning, rendering integration, optional workload or unverified older-target package route is required or advertised.
stabilityLimitations: Verified against .NET 11 RC2, not GA. These APIs are not publisher-designated experimental; no experimental opt-in is required.

evidence.scope: Real selective input binding and application-owned serialized reload worker; success, coalescing and caught failure.
Real ignored property and serialized Func<Task> callbacks, coalescing, caught async failure, synchronous propagation and completion after disposal.

humanProof.scope: Managed in-process claims need no Human-only proof. External services, distributed backends, browser/native behavior and GA reconciliation are not claimed. The LocalSize RC gap is explicit where applicable.
